title: The 1787 text defines treason and requires two witnesses or a confession
summary: The 1787 text defines treason and requires two witnesses or a confession.
body: Article III, Section 3 limits treason to levying war against the United States or adhering to their enemies, giving them aid and comfort, and requires the testimony of two witnesses to the same overt act, or a confession in open court, for a conviction. The source says: "Treason against the United States, shall consist only in levying War against them, or in adhering to their Enemies, giving them Aid and Comfort." The word 'only' is part of the definition. Congress may declare the punishment, but the transcription also bars corruption of blood or forfeiture beyond the life of the person attainted, in the words that follow the definition.
